title: Order service health indicators and probe groups
name: Order service health checks

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how the health endpoints and probe groups are configured? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The kitchen has 700 open tickets (threshold 500) and every other component is healthy. What does GET /actuator/health/readiness return?
choices: HTTP 503 with status DOWN, because any status other than UP fails the group
HTTP 200 with status DEGRADED, because the status order makes DEGRADED the aggregate and the http-mapping maps it to 200
HTTP 200 with status UP, because kitchenBacklog's detail values are not part of the aggregate
HTTP 200 with status OUT_OF_SERVICE, because the group falls back to its first indicator

questions.prompt: The Kafka brokers are unreachable. How long can OrderQueueHealthIndicator.health() block the thread handling the request?
choices: Indefinitely, because the AdminClient retries until a broker answers
Zero time, because the indicator reads a cached result
About 1.5 seconds, because the call is bounded by the timeout used in describeCluster and the future's get

questions.prompt: Why does health() restore the interrupt flag in the InterruptedException branch?
choices: Because Health.down(e) throws unless the thread is interrupted
So that the AdminClient is closed when the thread exits
So the code that owns the thread, for example the servlet container, can still see that it was asked to stop
To make the next health check run immediately on the same thread
